interest: Indexes 1940–43 controversies over Japanese American dual citizenship and expatriation.
keywords: United States v. Wong Kim Ark
overview: Decimal file 894.012 (File 117), titled 'Government. Mandates, Recognition., Japan, Citizenship. Divide As 130 To 139', consists of five pages of the Department of State's cumulative 'List of Papers' (docket register sheets) spanning July 1940 to November 1943, with a cover sheet dated October 12, 1945. Because records on Japanese citizenship and passport matters were divided and routed into the 130 decimal series (as well as related decimal classifications such as 134, 894.00, and 311.9415), this file contains no underlying correspondence or despatches, but rather indexes 28 numbered entries recording incoming and outgoing communications regarding Japanese nationality, dual citizenship of second-generation Japanese Americans (Nisei), expatriation procedures under Japanese law (especially in Hawaii), the impact of Section 402 of the Nationality Act of 1940, attempts by interned Japanese Americans at centers such as Rivers, Arizona, to renounce U.S. citizenship, diplomatic exchange of nationals via Switzerland and the Spanish Embassy, and constitutional debates over birthright citizenship and the Supreme Court precedent in United States v. Wong Kim Ark.

subfiles.about: Docket list of papers indexing correspondence, despatches, and legal memoranda concerning Japanese citizenship, dual nationality, expatriation, and wartime status under decimal file 894.012.
subfiles.summary: This five-page Department of State 'List of Papers' (docket register) compiles entries 35 through 62 of communications relating to Japanese citizenship and nationality accumulated between July 1940 and November 1943, with a cover sheet dated October 12, 1945. Because records on citizenship were divided into the 130 series, the register records document types, dates, senders, recipients, and purports with cross-references redirecting researchers to files such as 130-Japanese, 134-Hawaii, and related cases. Indexed matters include dual nationality of Nisei, simplified expatriation procedures requested by over 30,000 Japanese Americans in Hawaii, provisions of the Nationality Act of 1940, congressional proposals to revoke birthright citizenship, and legal opinions by Assistant Legal Adviser Richard W. Flournoy regarding Japanese nationality law and wartime renunciation of American citizenship by interned Japanese Americans.
